source.title: Reference intervals for reproductive hormones in prepubertal children on the automated Roche cobas e 411 analyzer
source.access: Full primary publication supplied by owner; Table 2 and assay/methods text checked against rendered PDF on 2026-10-10.
source.redistribution: Factual FSH medians, cohort metadata and citation only; publisher PDF and figures are not included.

population.recruitmentSite: University Hospital Center Sestre Milosrdnice, Zagreb
population.selection: Excluded suspected endocrinopathy, metabolic disorders, chronic diseases and interfering medications. Recruitment included acute respiratory infections or febrile illness, allergy testing and preoperative care; this was not a pure healthy volunteer cohort.

assay.method: Roche cobas e 411 electrochemiluminescence sandwich immunoassay
assay.material: Serum and Li-heparin plasma collected; analyte-specific matrix assignment is not reported.
assay.storage: Measured immediately or after storage at −20°C for no more than three months.

ageRouting.sourceBoundaryDefinition: Exact inclusive lower and exclusive upper age boundaries in Table 2.
ageRouting.applicationPolicy: Male 1–<6 years uses the published 1–<8-year median; preserve the existing Madsen 2022 age curve from 6 through 16 years. Female 1–<4, 4–<8 and 8–<11 years use their three separate published groups.
ageRouting.betweenGroups: No interpolation, smoothing or bridge between age-group medians or between publications.
ageRouting.minipuberty: No Zec profile under 1 year. Existing female infant FSH ends exclusively at 1 year to prevent overlap; all other Ljubicic analytes keep their current endpoint.

limitations: These are whole-group medians for children assessed as Tanner stage 1, not exact-age medians, continuous age trajectories or clinical reference limits.
Do not treat known pubertal children as part of the prepubertal reference cohort. Gonadal-stage eligibility must use the existing sex-specific puberty context, never inferred from age or FSH.
The boys 1–<6 application window is a source-priority policy, not a new source subgroup; median 0.48 IU/L and N=303 describe the full published 1–<8-year group.
Recruitment included pediatric outpatient and hospital visits, including acute illness; this was not a pure healthy-volunteer sample.
Serum and Li-heparin plasma were collected; the paper does not specify the matrix used for each hormone. No matrix-specific equivalence is established.
The assay belongs to the source cohort; automatic source selection does not establish the method or material of the patient sample, nor equivalence to other Roche assays or the Mayo FSH profile.
No gestational-age stratification is reported. These are not premature-infant reference data.
FSH group medians are quantifiable, but the study does not report a limit of quantification. LH and early-childhood testosterone medians are censored and are not activated by this extract.
The printed LH reference-limit inconsistency in Table 2 does not alter these FSH medians; no clinical reference limits are imported.

eligibility.context: Existing current-patient context only; a typed stage must be explicitly linked to the current context. No inference from age, FSH, generic Tanner, P or Ax, and no use of historical observations.
eligibility.missingOrIncompatibleStage: No Zec patient point; preserve separate clinical assessment when available.
eligibility.sexComparison: Do not use the patient’s gonadal stage to qualify the opposite sex. A comparison requiring Zec falls back to the existing schematic view.
